sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: claude-code-best-practice is a learning resource for Claude Code. It explains each building block, such as subagents, commands, skills, hooks, MCP servers, memory and settings, with a best-practice note and a working example in the repository.
sixtySeconds.problem: Claude Code has many features and it's hard to know how they fit together. This repo maps each one to where it lives (like .claude/agents or CLAUDE.md), links the official docs, and shows a full command to agent to skill workflow you can copy.
whoFor: Claude Code users moving beyond chat-style use
Developers building their own agent workflows
Teams writing CLAUDE.md and project settings
Learners who prefer examples over docs alone
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it as a structured course: concept tables with links, implementations you can run, and a large tips and tricks section to apply to your own project.

overview: The README is organised as tables. The Concepts table covers subagents, commands, skills, workflows, hooks, MCP servers, plugins, settings, status line, memory, checkpointing, sessions and the context window, each with its file location, official docs link and the repo's own best-practice and implementation notes. A Hot table tracks newer features.
The author suggests reading it as a course rather than installing it as a workflow. Running the /weather-orchestrator command shows a complete command, agent and skill flow you can use as a template.
There's also a tips and tricks section, sourced from the Claude team, that you can point Claude at to suggest improvements to your own CLAUDE.md. The repository is MIT licensed.
